widgets_values: Turn the character in <image1> into an orthographic 3D modeling reference sheet: a single horizontal row of four equal-width panels, evenly spaced. From left to right: 1) front view. 2) left side view, an exact 90° profile, snout pointing to the left edge of the image, only one eye visible, the near arm pointing straight at the camera and strongly foreshortened, the far arm hidden behind the body. 3) back view, exactly 180°. 4) right side view, an exact 90° profile, snout pointing to the right edge of the image, only one eye visible, near arm foreshortened toward the camera, far arm hidden. The camera orbits a completely static character: same T-pose and same head direction in every view, the character never turns toward the camera. Identical outfit, colors, proportions and scale in all views, each character centered in its panel, feet on the same baseline, no overlap between views. Flat, even lighting, solid black background, no text, no labels.

widgets_values: Turn the object in <image1> into an orthographic 3D modeling reference sheet: a single horizontal row of four equal-width panels, evenly spaced. From left to right: 1) front view. 2) left side view, an exact 90-degree profile. 3) back view, exactly 180 degrees. 4) right side view, an exact 90-degree profile. The camera orbits a completely static object: same orientation and shape in every view. Identical details, colors, materials, proportions and scale in all views, each subject centered in its panel with generous empty margins, aligned to the same baseline, no overlap between views. Flat, even lighting, solid black background, no text, no labels. Keep all attached components, handles, fasteners and openings in their fixed locations. Side views show the object's real thickness and depth. The back must be the corresponding rear surface and construction, not a mirrored front. Use a supplied rear reference for unseen construction when available.

widgets_values: Edit <image1> in place into a coherent finished product rendering sheet. All four panels depict the same object. The top-left panel is front, top-right is right side, bottom-left is back, bottom-right is left side, each from its existing slightly elevated camera. Preserve the exact panel boundaries and black separator gutters. Keep every object at its existing position, size and tilt inside its own panel. Preserve each panel silhouette, body proportions, camera perspective, visible surfaces, attachment positions and occlusion from <image1>. Restore crisp finished materials, colors and surface ornament using <image2> for identity and <image3> for appearance around the object. Keep the neutral gray panel backgrounds and black gutters unchanged, with one complete object in each panel. Keep details attached to the corresponding surfaces and consistent across views; rear-facing surfaces retain rear-facing presentation. The appearance references supply material and detail contributions; the four existing panels supply all target viewpoints and framing. Asset description: . Additional preservation instructions: Preserve the distinctive parts and their attachment positions across all views.. The structural condition supplies matching depth for these exact four panels. The edit mask identifies the object region to finish. Transfer appearance onto the corresponding visible surfaces; preserve the primary geometry and each existing viewpoint. The guide supplies the camera, outer silhouette and major body proportions. Rebuild rough proxy surface details as finished materials and ornament from the appearance references; do not interpret proxy noise or faceting as intentional decoration. Structural depth can still constrain geometry; any incorrect controlled surface requires a separate masked correction. Reference roles: <image1>: The editing canvas: four measured Blender camera frames and black separator gutters. <image2>: Original identity, materials, palette and ornament; appearance reference. <image3>: Concept appearance around this same object; colors and surface details, with approximate geometry.
